scope: Shared damage-event multiplier trace and projectile effect bindings; partial runtime recovery, not complete simulation
findings: Both projectile damage effects select PredExecutionCalculation_Damage.
The native capture definition identifies TempOnHitPerc. Its damage-path local starts at 1 and is passed to captured-attribute evaluation; this is not proof that every attack evaluates to 1.

The resulting float is copied into the reflected GameplayEventDataObject.EventDataFloat field and assigned to GameplayEventData.OptionalObject2. That object is retained in the Event.OnDamageDealt payload. Sky Splitter and other recovered Blueprint passives read that field.

Scattershot selects an attribute-based TempDamage modifier sourced from AttackDamage, a TempOnHitPerc override, and a lane-minion-only TempDamage multiplier. Their curve bindings are distinct; inactive magnitude arms must not be counted as extra damage.

At curve inputs zero or one, the recovered Scattershot bindings give 0.4 attack-damage scaling, 0.5 on-hit percentage, 1.5 lane-minion multiplier, and 0.65-second cooldown. Its serialized targeting radius is 650 world units. Projectile effect level and final native composition still require validation.
Onixian binds attack-damage scaling and a custom distance magnitude. Its unused post-additive curve row has a null table; the row name alone is not a valid extra damage binding.

The shared native critical path requires the CanCriticallyStrike tag, a further unresolved enum gate, positive evaluated OverrideCriticalChance and a valid owning object. On success it marks CriticalDamage and multiplies the current damage term by 1 plus evaluated CriticalBonus. This does not establish final mitigation order or a universal bonus default.

The decision helper clamps finite chance inputs to zero through one. Interior chances use persistent success/failure counters, cached coefficients for the chance and its complement, and a random comparison. A success increments the success counter and clears failures; a failure increments failures and clears successes. This is stateful, not independent fixed-probability rolls.

The coefficient helper uses a bounded numerical search over a weighted waiting-time calculation. Constants and reachable branches were inspected privately, but constructor initialization and the imported random function are now traced; reset boundaries and cross-effect sharing remain open.

The critical decision state belongs to PredAbilitySystemComponent. Its registered constructor initializes the failure counter to 1 and success counter to 0. This establishes construction-time initialization only, not the state on spawn, respawn or the first attack of a selected fight.

The random comparison calls the named C runtime rand import. The masking and floating-point scaling were inspected privately. Runtime seed, global stream interactions and server implementation parity remain unverified.
limits: Native execution was located through class construction and its overridden virtual slot. Reachable instructions and reflection layouts are private; static tracing is not server-parity validation.

Critical-strike eligibility and stateful decision structure are partially traced; post-construction state lifecycle/reset, full modifier aggregation, healing, target selection/collision and downstream passive behavior remain incomplete.
The default event multiplier must not be generalized to every event producer or bypass effect overrides.
No projectile damage credit or automatic winning-build claim is introduced.

Production basicHit still computes an average crit contribution. These traces do not validate short-window crit sequences or justify replacing that average with guessed initial state. No new critical probability or multiplier constant is introduced.
